newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Gas Oil/Jet - Steady as IOC seeks less diesel.
newsitem.headline: Asia Gas Oil/Jet - Steady as IOC seeks less diesel.

text.p: Singapore physical gas oil market appeared to have consolidated for now but traders said the undertone remained soft especially since India was expected to take less than expected volumes for March.
They noted that the 100,000 tonnes that a European major has been offering these past two days attest to the abundant supplies in Singapore which are seeking homes.

The major offered four cargoes on Friday at around $26.00 per tonne, free-on-board (fob) around the same level that they started offering at on Thursday but higher than the $25.20 deal traded between a local trader and a Dutch trader.
The seller again offered today at $25.80, which was later lowered to $25.40 for a mid-February cargo with three bids seen at that level and another at $25.00.
But gas oil swaps largely ignored talk that India would take 500,000-600,000 tonnes of gas oil in its tender for March deliveries, down from earlier expectations of 600,000-900,000 tonnes.

Traders said talk of some activity in gas oil sales in Hong Kong to China and Indonesia's demand helped to limit a further fall. A Japanese trader was recently said to have sold a gas oil cargo into China at $210 per tonne cost-and-freight basis.
A US major was said to have sold a 20,000-tonne cargo to a US trader recently at a 30-cent-per-barrel discount to Singapore spot quotes fob.
Traders said a South Korean refiner this week sold two jet fuel cargoes into Japan, fob basis.
One cargo was sold at $1.10 a barrel over Singapore spot quotes to a Swiss trader who has a commitment to a Japanese refiner. The second cargo was sold at a $1.00-premium.
Jet fuel prices continued to command a premium of $2.60-$3.00 a barrel over gas oil, reflecting sustained demand for jet.
